scope: Proposition 5.7 (Virtual product marginals) of the manuscript “The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture” (preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 022 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d91ccb7b68c5b0e2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each retained good row, there is a nonnegative virtual weight on its true numerator grid with the following properties. 1. It dominates the actual final weight, and its first mass lies between chardϕ(v)r(v) and ϕ(v)r(v). 2. Its total excess over the actual final first mass is exactly accounted for by the first-moment discard losses in the projected tables, when the virtual weight omits the soft and additional static tests, cap clipping, and partition discards. 3. At fixed static anchor choices, every subset of the actual hard and adaptive fields has mean equal to the product of its local means. An actual hard field has mean 1 − bp/p when it forbids bp ≤ 2 distinct residues, or mean Rp when it is a prescribed scalar; adaptive full fields have mean Rp. For upper counts one may retain just one hard birth exclusion at each applicable prime, or the scalar Rp when there is no exclusion. Any subset of the resulting hard and adaptive fields has the product of its ordinary local means. 4. Fields through a prime p, restricted to a later projection of denominator v′, have a joint period dividing v′ of size at most exp(O(p)). Domination in the first item is after the static anchor average; it is not required separately for each auxiliary anchor choice.
